chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abdullah ibn Talhah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "The fasting person is in a state of worship, even if he is on his bed, as long as he does not backbite a Muslim."
ai.seo_question: Does a fasting person remain in worship if they are resting in bed?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores that the spiritual merit of fasting is continuous and not confined to active worship, provided the fast is not invalidated by backbiting (*ghibtah*). This highlights the Shia emphasis on *akhlaq* (ethics) as an integral component of *ibadah*, where preserving the honor of others is as critical as abstaining from food and drink. The hadith serves as a practical guide for maintaining the sanctity of the fast throughout all daily activities, including rest.
